primary.title: Mein Kampf
primary.author: Adolf Hitler
primary.rationale: Hitler's autobiographical manifesto outlining his political ideology and future plans for Germany. It is a foundational text for understanding his worldview.

primary.title: Speeches of Adolf Hitler, 1925-1945
primary.author: Adolf Hitler
primary.rationale: A collection of Hitler's public addresses, offering direct insight into his propaganda, political strategies, and public persona.

primary.title: Hitler's Table Talk
primary.author: Adolf Hitler
primary.rationale: Transcripts of Hitler's informal monologues and conversations during mealtimes, providing insights into his personal thoughts and opinions, though subject to interpretation by the transcriber.

secondary.title: Hitler: A Biography
secondary.author: Ian Kershaw
secondary.rationale: Considered the definitive modern biography of Hitler, this two-volume work provides a comprehensive and scholarly analysis of his life, rise to power, and regime.

secondary.title: The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich: A History of Nazi Germany
secondary.author: William L. Shirer
secondary.rationale: While published before 1976, this is a seminal and widely respected historical account of Nazi Germany, offering extensive context for Hitler's actions and policies. Later editions and analyses often build upon or discuss its findings.

secondary.title: Hitler's Willing Executioners: Ordinary Germans and the Holocaust
secondary.author: Daniel Jonah Goldhagen
secondary.rationale: A controversial but influential work that examines the role of ordinary Germans in the Holocaust, providing a critical perspective on the societal context of Hitler's regime.

suggestions.notes: Primary source availability on Wikisource and Project Gutenberg for Adolf Hitler's works is limited. Internet Archive is a more likely repository for his writings and speeches. The secondary source by William L. Shirer, though older, remains a foundational text in the field and is often referenced in later scholarship.
